record.draft:
title: "First apprentice"
excerpt: 'Northfold is taking on its first apprentice in January. Two years on site and in the studio, no degree needed, and applications close on 30 November.'
category: news
body: |-
  We're taking on an apprentice. It's the first time Northfold has done this, it starts in January, and it runs for two years. You don't need a degree, just a real wish to get into garden design and landscaping. Letters need to reach us by 30 November.

  We've never done this before. We're rather looking forward to it.

  ## What the two years involve

  You'll split your time between site and the design office. On site, that's the real work of making a garden: digging the soil pit we dig on every project, setting out beds, planting, and going back later to see what has thrived and what has sulked. In the office, it's surveys, drawings and planting plans, and we start those by hand before anything goes near a screen.

  You'll learn by doing, alongside the rest of us, on real gardens for real people.

  ## Who we're looking for

  Someone curious and practical. You don't need a degree. You might be leaving school. You might be changing career. You might be the person friends ring when their roses look poorly, who has never quite had the chance to do it properly.

  What matters is that you notice things, ask why, and don't mind muddy knees. Most of our gardens are in Northumberland, so you'll need to be local, or happy to become so.

  ## How to apply

  There's no form. Just write us a short letter about one thing:

  **A garden or landscape you love, and why.**

  It can be famous, or it can be your gran's back yard. A page is plenty. We'd much rather hear what you noticed than read a list of what you've done.

  Send it to the studio by **30 November**. If you have questions before then, get in touch. We're happy to chat.

  And if someone you know should read this, please pass it on.

  We don't know yet who will write to us, or which garden they'll choose. That's the part we're most looking forward to. Will we do it again? Ask us in two years.
